transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-10-05
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Sequoia Head of ML), Tom (Platform), Priya (Security), Mark (SRE), Janelle (Product)

Summary/Opening:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um we wanted to walk through the kickoff plan for the onboarding, confirm the pilot scope and next steps. very excited to have Sequoia on board. 
[00:20] Aisha: hi all, yep thanks, we are keen to get the inference pipeline stabilized. primary goals are sub-150ms 99th pct for our chat assistants and keeping unit cost under our current baseline.

Transcript body:
[01:01] Diego: quick intro, im Diego, I'm the systems engineer who'll own the pilot setup and perf harness, i'll coordinate with Tom on networking. quick confirm — are we leaning Dedicated or private deploy for the pilot?
[01:18] Tom: leaning Dedicated to start, yes — we need predictability before we commit to full private infra. Also want to validate autoscale and burst behavior.
[01:30] Priya: from security side we have a checklist: SSO SAML, audit logs, kms integration, data residency. we'll need SOC2 docs and detail on how logs are stored — retention and access controls.
[01:47] Samir: totally, we've got a security pack — i'll share SOC2 scan and our KMS integration guide. For Dedicated we provide customer-isolated pools and optional private control plane; we can support customer-managed KMS or our managed KMS depending on your compliance appetite.
[02:10] Janelle: timeline question — what's realistic? We have a product milestone end of October and would like the pilot done before then.
[02:22] Leah: ok doable — proposal: provision Dedicated trial the week of Oct 16, run 1 week of controlled traffic, SE runs bench and we review metrics and quality checks. that should give you a go/no-go by end Oct.
[02:40] Mark: about networking — we prefer VPC peering rather than open internet egress; any special egress rules?
[02:52] Diego: yes we recommend peering or PrivateLink. For peering we need your VPC CIDR ranges and a few allowlisted IPs for the staging cluster. also please confirm whether you require fixed egress IPs for outbound webhooks.
[03:12] Tom: i'll pull CIDR and the current firewall rules. We might want to do egress through a NAT gateway — is that supported?
[03:22] Diego: yes NAT is fine, just provide the egress IPs that will be allowed. note: if you use VPC peering there is some transient routing when we scale nodes, we document that in the runbook.

[05:00] Diego: on perf and models — what's your typical seq length and token distribution? do you have caching/prefix patterns?
[05:12] Aisha: average convo length is about 80 tokens but we have long tails up to 800 tokens on some support cases. We do prefix system prompts and keep session KV caches. we care about KV cache rehydration perf.
[05:38] Diego: ok good, that's helpful. we'll configure KV cache sizes and advise quantization profiles. for latency, we can tune batching and continuous batching to hit 99th pct targets; tradeoff is cost uplift.
[05:52] Samir: also Redwood Optimize will give recommendations on batching+quant profiles once the pilot runs. we'll show token-level cost breakdowns so you can decide.

[08:20] Priya: on encryption — does Redwood's dedicated offering allow customer-managed keys/hsm? we need HSM-backed keys for PII pipeline.
[08:35] Samir: yes we have KMS integrations and an HSM option for Private deploys; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (customer-managed). i'll follow up with the KMS integration doc.

[10:05] Janelle: quality/regressions — how will we detect regressions vs model drift during pilot?
[10:17] Leah: we ask customers to bring 50-100 prompt tests; Redwood Optimize can flag quality regressions across these prompt sets. we'll hook your evals into the pipeline and alarm on metric drift.
[10:35] Aisha: good — we'll prepare an initial eval set.

[12:00] Samir: a quick note on pricing/committing — Dedicated has reserved monthly blocks, pilot is charged at trial rates but will show expected run rate based on tokens. i'll send the pricing sheet after this call.
[12:18] Tom: are there hidden costs for model variants or fallback routing? we want to understand unit economics if we fall back to hosted during load spikes.
[12:30] Diego: fallback can add latency and cost; we can set routing policies to prefer cheaper variants with sane timeouts. we'll show cost impact in the dashboard.

[15:00] Mark: operationally, who will get access to logs and traces? we need granular RBAC and audit trails.
[15:15] Leah: Console supports token-level audit logs and RBAC via SSO groups; we'll map your roles to console RBAC during onboarding. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[15:30] Priya: can audit logs be retained 13 months? compliance team requires 12 months plus buffer.
[15:40] Samir: default retention is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an add-on — we'll include retention options in the docs.

[18:00] Diego: technical deep dive note: for your long-tail sequences we'll recommend a model variant with mixed-precision quant and an optimized kernel selection. continuous KV cache will reduce repeated prefix cost.
[18:20] Aisha: what's the expected token-cost reduction from caching?
[18:27] Diego: depends, but prefix caching can be 20-40% savings for sessions with repeated contexts; we'll share an example calc in the runbook.

[22:45] Leah: owner assignments — i'll own the weekly cadences and onboarding checklist; Samir will own commercial and pilot pricing; Diego will own bench and infra; Priya will own security Qs from Sequoia.
[23:05] Samir: noted. action items and due dates we'll put in the doc.

[30:00] (brief crosstalk about calendar availability)

[35:00] Aisha: can you run a small smoke test with a single model variant before full pilot? maybe a 2-hour short-run to sanity check routing and keys.
[35:12] Diego: yes we can. we'll do a smoke run once we have network access and SSO creds. ideally that happens the week before the pilot.

[42:00] Priya: regarding legal/process — we will need DPA and a list of subprocessors. any unusual subprocessors?
[42:12] Samir: we'll send the DPA and current subprocessors list; no unusual ones outside major cloud providers. legal might want extra clauses for data residency — we'll loop in the contracts team if needed.

[48:30] Tom: when you say private control plane for Private deploys — how much ops overhead is on our side vs Redwood?
[48:42] Diego: for Private on-prem we ship a package and you manage infra, but we provide orchestration and support. for VPC Private deployments we offer a light control plane that can be customer-hosted; details in the Private deployment guide. we'll tailor by engagement.

[52:00] Leah: recap and next steps — re-state: Samir sends pricing and security pack; Diego will prepare bench harness and run smoke test; Tom will share networking info; Priya sends security questionnaire answers; Leah will schedule the kickoff for pilot on Oct 16.
[52:25] Janelle: fine with that. thanks all.
[52:35] Samir: thanks everyone we'll follow up by EOD with docs.
[52:45] Aisha: thanks. bye.

End of transcript.
